title: How to build a training pilot that can support a buying decision
summary: Plan a training pilot with clear readiness criteria, a credible baseline and evidence that supports a decision to expand, change or stop.
body_markdown:
A convincing demo shows that an exercise works. A useful pilot shows whether it addresses the training problem your business needs to solve. Agree the decision before choosing the exercises.


## Start with the operational problem


Choose a role, a workflow and a current constraint. That might be new hires needing frequent help during nesting, trainer capacity limiting practice, or a client programme waiting for people to become competent. Avoid trying to prove every possible benefit in one pilot.


## Record the baseline and the comparison


Define what proficiency means before measuring it: which tasks people must complete, which errors are unacceptable and how much support is permitted. Record the current journey and trainer effort. If you compare cohorts, document differences in experience, workload and instruction; do not attribute every change to the new tool.


## Measure performance and effort separately


Observe representative tasks, time to a readiness checkpoint and the help learners still require. Separately record authoring, review, assignment and coaching time. Usage tells you whether people participated; it does not, by itself, show proficiency or financial return.


## Make the business case conservative


Estimate value from the capacity you can actually use. A saved trainer hour is capacity returned, not automatically a cash saving. For an outsourced programme, check when the contract starts paying for a competent representative. Do not count the same productive time as both saved cost and additional revenue.


## Agree a decision record


Write down the owner, cohort, tasks, baseline, success criteria, review date, total cost and unresolved risks. End with a recommendation to expand, change the programme or stop. In a Solidroad evaluation, ask to review the learner evidence and trainer workflow against these same criteria.
